# Field

> A label wired up to a control of your own. Bring any input, select, or element you like.

`<slab-field>` · Form · built on `<label>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/field/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/field.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-field required>
  <label>Website</label>
  <input slot="control" type="url" />
  <span slot="description">Where people can find you.</span>
</slab-field>
```

## Elements

### `<slab-field>`

Import `slab-elements/field.js` to register it.

A label and the control it names, with no visual styles.

Field wires the two together. Both are slotted, so they're in the same tree and no ID reference has to cross a shadow root: Field gives the control an `id` and points the label's `for` at it. A `for` or an `id` that's already set is left alone, so a consumer who wants to wire it themselves can.

The control is described by each element slotted into `description`, through its `aria-describedby`, after any IDs it already has. And `error` sets its `aria-invalid`, so a screenreader says it's invalid and reads the description that says why.

Beyond that, what Field provides is a place for each piece and custom states for what a design needs to know about them: `:state(disabled)`, `:state(error)`, and `:state(required)`.

`required` renders nothing. A design that wants an asterisk adds one from outside, through `::part(label)`. Layout is the same: where the label sits relative to its control is for the styles around it, not for this class.

`hide-label` hides the label visually and leaves it where screenreaders and a `<label for>` can still reach it.

#### Attributes

| Name         | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `disabled`   | `boolean` | `false` | Matches `:state(disabled)`, for styles. Disable the control itself too.                                                                    |
| `error`      | `boolean` | `false` | Sets the control's `aria-invalid`, so a screenreader says it's invalid and reads the description saying why. Also matches `:state(error)`. |
| `hide-label` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                           |
| `required`   | `boolean` | `false` | Matches `:state(required)`, for styles such as an asterisk. Make the control itself required too.                                          |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default)     | `Element \| string` |                                                                                                          |
| `control`     | `Element`           | The control the label names, such as an `<input>`. It's given an `id` and is described by `description`. |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Text that describes the control, through its `aria-describedby`.                                         |

#### CSS parts

| Name          | Description                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `control`     | The control the label names                        |
| `description` | Text about the control, such as a hint or an error |
| `label`       | The label                                          |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                              |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While `disabled` is set.                                 |
| `:state(error)`    | While `error` is set.                                    |
| `:state(required)` | While `required` is set, for styles such as an asterisk. |
